data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 proposes recovery-time variance as the distinguishing evidence but its mechanism conflates recovery dynamics with failure-independence structure. The 'step-function recovery tied to a single external fix' is a property of the remediation process, not of whether the failures themselves were truly independent. Its own countercondition exposes this: if independent services' recoveries are centrally coordinated by a third party, they can also exhibit a step-function restoration, destroying the proposed discriminator. Conversely, independent services that all consume the same upstream dependency can independently fail and then all recover when that upstream is restored, producing the same step-function pattern without the failures being correlated in origin. The mechanism therefore fails to causally distinguish hidden shared-cause failures from independent failures sharing a common remediation trigger.
